alerts.title: Fall Armyworm Outbreak — Gulu District
alerts.description: Severe Fall Armyworm infestation detected across maize fields in Gulu and Amuru districts. Larvae at 3rd instar stage. Immediate action required.

alerts.title: Dry Spell Alert — Karamoja Sub-Region
alerts.description: UNMA forecast indicates a 3-week dry spell in Moroto and Kotido. Soil moisture levels critically low. Delay planting of second-season beans.

alerts.title: Coffee Leaf Rust Detected — Rwenzori Region
alerts.description: NARO plant health surveillance confirms Hemileia vastatrix (Coffee Leaf Rust) in Kasese and Kabarole. Estimated 18% canopy affected. Apply copper fungicide within 48 hours.

alerts.title: Maize Farm-Gate Price Rise — Eastern Uganda
alerts.description: UBOS district price monitoring shows maize farm-gate prices up 22% in Mbale and Iganga over the past two weeks due to reduced cross-border supply from Kenya.

alerts.title: Flash Flood Risk — Lake Victoria Crescent
alerts.description: UNMA issues flash flood warning for Wakiso, Mukono, and Kalangala. Banana and coffee gardens near drainage channels at risk. Avoid field operations for 72 hours.

crops.name: Coffee (Robusta)
crops.description: Uganda's leading export crop, grown mainly in the Highlands and Lake Victoria crescent. Robusta thrives in humid lowland zones at 1,000–1,500 m elevation.
crops.season: Biannual — main harvest Oct–Feb, fly crop May–Aug

crops.name: Maize
crops.description: The most widely grown staple in Uganda, cultivated across all agro-ecological zones. A core food-security and income crop for smallholder farmers.

crops.name: Beans
crops.description: A critical protein source and cash crop for millions of Ugandan households. Common bean varieties include K132, NABE 15, and climbing beans for highland zones.

crops.name: Bananas (Matooke)
crops.description: Uganda is Africa's largest banana producer. Matooke (East African Highland Banana) is both the staple food and a major cash crop, especially in the Buganda and Western regions.

crops.name: Cassava
crops.description: A drought-tolerant food security crop grown across northern and eastern Uganda. Improved varieties like NASE 14 offer high yield and resistance to Cassava Brown Streak Disease.
crops.season: Planted at onset of rains — harvested 9–18 months later

farming_practices.title: Integrated Soil Fertility Management for Maize
farming_practices.description: Combine mineral fertiliser (50 kg/ha NPK) with 2 tonnes/ha well-composted farmyard manure. Apply at planting in Season A. Validated by NARO Namulonge for Lake Victoria Crescent soils.

farming_practices.title: Coffee Shade Management for Robusta Yield
farming_practices.description: Maintain 30–40% shade canopy using Grevillea robusta or Calliandra. Shade reduces temperature stress and improves bean quality. Prune shade trees annually after main harvest.

farming_practices.title: Climbing Bean Staking in Southwest Highlands
farming_practices.description: Use 2 m eucalyptus stakes for climbing bean varieties (K132, MAC 44). Stake at 3rd node stage. Yield improvement of 60–80% over bush beans. Cost-effective when stakes are sourced locally.

farming_practices.title: Hass Avocado Orchard Establishment Guide
farming_practices.description: Plant on 6m × 6m spacing on terraced hillsides. Use grafted Hass on Guatemalan rootstock. Apply 200g DAP per hole at planting. Irrigate during dry spells in first two years. Target altitude: 1400–2000 m.

farming_practices.title: Conservation Agriculture for Cassava — Gulu Sub-Region
farming_practices.description: Minimum tillage with mulching using maize stover reduces soil moisture loss by 35% in dry spells. Plant improved varieties NASE 14 or TME 14. Intercrop with groundnuts for income diversification.

field_visits.observations: Coffee showing early signs of leaf rust on lower canopy. Shade trees overgrown — recommend pruning. Soil moisture adequate. Farmer applying mulch correctly.
field_visits.advisories_given: Apply copper oxychloride 50% WP at 40g/20L water. Prune shade trees to restore 30% canopy. Rogue two diseased stems.
field_visits.follow_up_actions: Return in 3 weeks to assess fungicide efficacy and verify shade management corrective action.

field_visits.observations: Cassava plot in Lira showing mosaic virus symptoms on 15% of stand. Volunteer weeds competing significantly. No signs of whitefly population above threshold.
field_visits.advisories_given: Remove and destroy symptomatic plants. Plant certified NASE 14 cuttings in gaps. Apply mulch to suppress weeds and conserve moisture.
field_visits.follow_up_actions: Coordinate with NARO Abi to arrange certified planting material supply for Lira sub-county.

field_visits.observations: Maize in whorl stage. Fall Armyworm frass visible in 4 of 20 sampled plants — approaching economic threshold. Farmer has emamectin benzoate in store but needs guidance on dosage.
field_visits.advisories_given: Apply Emamectin Benzoate 1.9% EC at 10ml/20L water. Spray into whorl at 7-day intervals for two applications. Wear PPE — gloves and mask.
field_visits.follow_up_actions: Verify pest population reduction 10 days post-spray. Report to MAAIF district extension office if population persists.

field_visits.observations: Second visit — cassava plot partially re-planted with NASE 14. Weeding completed on 1.2 ha. Soil compaction noted on access path — advise cover cropping.
field_visits.advisories_given: Intercrop with groundnuts on 0.5 ha for soil improvement and income diversification. Apply 30 kg/ha CAN at 6 weeks after planting.
field_visits.follow_up_actions: Confirm groundnut variety selected. Submit yield data to NARO monitoring programme.

field_visits.observations: Beans at flowering stage. Bean fly damage noted at 8% incidence. Farmer delayed seed treatment — advise immediate foliar spray. Plot area: 1.5 acres.
field_visits.advisories_given: Apply Imidacloprid 200 SL at 5ml/20L as foliar spray. Repeat at 14 days. Record incidence at each visit for MAAIF seasonal pest data.
field_visits.follow_up_actions: Assess pod set and bean fly incidence at pod-filling stage in 3 weeks.

pest_alerts.description: Fall Armyworm larvae at 3rd–4th instar stage confirmed in maize fields. Characteristic 'window-pane' feeding damage on leaves. Populations exceeding economic threshold of 1 larva per 5 plants.
pest_alerts.scouting_action: Scout at least 20 random plants per acre. Check whorls for frass and feeding damage. Count larvae per plant.
pest_alerts.treatment_options: Emamectin Benzoate 1.9% EC (10ml/20L), Chlorpyrifos 48% EC (30ml/20L). Apply at early morning or evening. Rotate chemistries to prevent resistance.
pest_alerts.triggered_by: UNMA rainfall anomaly + pheromone trap count > 50/week

pest_alerts.description: Coffee Berry Borer infestation rate above 5% in sampled berries. Risk heightened by prolonged wet conditions. Post-harvest sanitation and removal of mummified berries critical to break the cycle.
pest_alerts.scouting_action: Collect 200 berries from random trees in the plot. Dissect and count infested berries. Calculate infestation rate %.
pest_alerts.treatment_options: Beauveria bassiana biopesticide (NARO-approved). Chemical option: Endosulfan 35% EC where registered. Harvest all ripe berries within 2 weeks.
pest_alerts.triggered_by: Sentinel Hub moisture index > 0.7 for 14 consecutive days

pest_alerts.description: Bean fly adults detected at early seedling emergence stage. Larvae mine stems causing wilting and stand loss. Risk highest in Season A under dry conditions post-planting.
pest_alerts.scouting_action: Observe 25 seedlings (5–14 DAS) per 0.1 ha. Check for yellow cotyledons, swollen stem base, and maggots inside stem.
pest_alerts.treatment_options: Seed treatment with thiamethoxam 35% FS before planting. Foliar spray: Imidacloprid 200 SL at 5 ml/20L at 7 and 14 DAS.
pest_alerts.triggered_by: NARO pest monitoring network — Kabale sub-region

pest_alerts.description: Banana Xanthomonas Wilt (Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum) confirmed in Masindi district. Symptoms include premature ripening, internal fruit discolouration, and wilting of male buds. Highly contagious.
pest_alerts.scouting_action: Inspect all mats for yellow leaf margins, premature bunch yellowing, and oozing latex. Rogue symptomatic plants immediately.
pest_alerts.treatment_options: No chemical cure. Single stem removal (SSR) of infected stems. Disinfect tools with 10% bleach between plants. Destroy male buds at banana emergence to prevent insect spread.
pest_alerts.triggered_by: MAAIF plant health surveillance report — Masindi County

pest_alerts.description: Cassava Brown Streak Virus detected in Lira district through NARO diagnostic lab. Causes necrotic streaking on green stems and root necrosis rendering tubers inedible. Whitefly-transmitted.
pest_alerts.scouting_action: Check for yellow-green leaf mottling, green stem streaking, and root decay at harvest. Send samples to NARO Namulonge for PCR confirmation.
pest_alerts.treatment_options: Plant certified virus-free cuttings (NASE 14, TME 14). Control whitefly vectors with mineral oil sprays. Rogue and destroy infected plants. Practice clean-seed village multiplication.
pest_alerts.triggered_by: NARO Abi Station field survey — Lira sub-region

recommendations.title: Apply Bean Fly Treatment Before Seedling Stage
recommendations.description: UNMA forecast predicts dry conditions at planting in Kabale — ideal for bean fly emergence. Apply seed treatment before planting Season B.
recommendations.recommended_action: Treat bean seed with thiamethoxam 35% FS at 7g/kg seed before planting.

recommendations.title: Delay Planting — Short Dry Spell Forecast for Mbarara
recommendations.description: UNMA 7-day forecast shows below-average rainfall for Mbarara. Delay bean planting by 7–10 days to avoid poor germination.
recommendations.recommended_action: Wait for the next rainfall event before planting. Monitor UNMA updates daily.

recommendations.title: Anthracnose Risk High — Eastern Highlands
recommendations.description: High humidity forecast (>85%) over 10 days in Mbale and Sironko creates ideal conditions for bean anthracnose outbreak.
recommendations.triggering_forecast: Sentinel Hub Moisture Index anomaly — Eastern Highlands
recommendations.recommended_action: Scout fields for dark lesions on pods and stems. Apply Mancozeb 80% WP at first sign of infection.

recommendations.title: Low Soil pH Detected — Kabale Highland Zone
recommendations.description: IoT sensors and NARO soil survey indicate pH below 5.5 in Kabale highland plots. Beans require pH 6.0–7.0 for optimum yield.
recommendations.triggering_forecast: IoT soil pH sensor network — Kabale
recommendations.recommended_action: Apply agricultural lime at 2 tonnes/ha 6 weeks before planting. Retest pH after 4 weeks.

recommendations.title: CBSV Risk Elevated — Lira and Apac Districts
recommendations.description: NARO Abi surveillance and whitefly trap counts above threshold in Lira sub-region indicate elevated Cassava Brown Streak Virus transmission risk.
recommendations.recommended_action: Use only certified NASE 14 or TME 14 planting material. Spray mineral oil to suppress whitefly populations.

seasonal_calendars.notes: Season A beans in Kabale and Kisoro. Use climbing varieties (K132, MAC 44) with staking. Watch for bean fly at seedling emergence.
Plant at onset of long rains in Gulu, Lira, Apac. Use certified NASE 14 cuttings. Harvest at 9–12 months for best starch content.
Main Robusta harvest in Mukono, Wakiso, Masaka. Scout for Coffee Berry Borer weekly from berry formation. Wet-process cherries within 12 hours of harvest.
Season B cassava in Iganga, Tororo, Pallisa. Intercrop with groundnuts for soil improvement. Monitor for whitefly vectors of CBSV.
Fly crop harvest in Kasese, Kamwenge, Fort Portal. Lower volume than main crop. Prioritise shade management and post-harvest quality control.

treatments.scouting_action: Inspect mats weekly for yellowing leaves, premature bunch ripening, and oozing bacterial exudate from cut stems.
treatments.chemical_treatment: No chemical cure. Remove and destroy infected stems immediately.
treatments.biological_treatment: Single stem removal (SSR). Disinfect tools with 10% bleach solution between mats.
treatments.cultural_practice: Destroy male buds at flower emergence to prevent insect spread. Plant certified disease-free suckers only.

treatments.scouting_action: Scout 20 plants/acre at whorl stage. Check whorls for frass. Action threshold: 1 larva per 5 plants.
treatments.chemical_treatment: Emamectin Benzoate 1.9% EC at 10ml/20L. Chlorpyrifos 48% EC at 30ml/20L. Spray into whorl at 7-day intervals.
treatments.biological_treatment: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) formulations at early larval stage. Push-pull intercropping with Desmodium and Napier grass.
treatments.cultural_practice: Early planting at onset of rains to avoid peak moth flight. Deep tillage to destroy pupae in soil.

treatments.scouting_action: Observe 25 seedlings per 0.1 ha at 5–14 DAS. Check for swollen stem base, yellowing cotyledons, and larvae inside stem.
treatments.chemical_treatment: Imidacloprid 200 SL at 5ml/20L as foliar spray at 7 and 14 DAS.
treatments.biological_treatment: Seed treatment with thiamethoxam 35% FS at 7g/kg before planting.
treatments.cultural_practice: Avoid late planting into dry conditions. Use certified bean seed. Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest.

treatments.scouting_action: Collect 200 berries from random trees. Dissect and count infested berries. Economic threshold: 5% infestation.
treatments.chemical_treatment: Endosulfan 35% EC (where registered). Spray at early berry stage. Rotate with Chlorpyrifos.
treatments.biological_treatment: Beauveria bassiana biopesticide (NARO-approved strain). Apply at onset of berry boring season.
treatments.cultural_practice: Harvest all ripe berries within 2 weeks. Collect fallen berries (mummies). Improve shade management.

treatments.scouting_action: Check for yellow-green leaf mottling, brown streaking on green stems, and root necrosis at harvest. Submit samples to NARO Namulonge for PCR confirmation.
treatments.chemical_treatment: No direct chemical treatment. Mineral oil (2%) sprays to suppress whitefly vector populations.
treatments.biological_treatment: Parasitoid wasps for whitefly biological control (NARO research programme).
treatments.cultural_practice: Plant only certified NASE 14 or TME 14 cuttings. Rogue infected plants. Practice clean-seed village multiplication.

crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.description: NDVI changepoint detected. 15% canopy decline over 3 weeks correlated with Coffee Leaf Rust spread pattern.
crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.recommended_action: Apply copper-based fungicide immediately. Increase UAV monitoring to bi-weekly.

crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.description: Mann-Kendall trend analysis shows statistically significant NDVI decline (p<0.01). Fall Armyworm infestation confirmed in 15% of surveyed area.
crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.recommended_action: Deploy pheromone traps. Apply approved insecticide within 48 hours. Alert neighbouring farms.

crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.description: Soil moisture sensor readings dropped below 35% threshold for 9 consecutive days. EVI index declining.
crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.recommended_action: Activate supplemental irrigation if available. Apply mulching to conserve soil moisture.

crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.description: Spectral anomaly in UAV imagery. Xanthomonas Wilt signature detected in 12% of plantation with upward trend.
crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.recommended_action: Immediately rogue affected mats. Disinfect tools. Notify district agricultural officer.

crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.description: Minor deviation from seasonal NDVI baseline detected. Likely heavy cloud cover affecting Sentinel-2 readings.
crop_monitoring__timeseries_alerts.recommended_action: Re-acquire cloud-free imagery in 5 days to confirm crop health status.
